title: AI Mismatches: Identifying Potential Algorithmic Harms Before AI Development

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative early-stage risk assessment using the 'Disparate Performance' and 'Model Unobservables' matrices to anticipate expected performance gaps and ethical costs before AI development (e.g., applied to child welfare screening and healthcare case studies).

Anticipatory conceptual evaluation using the framework's risk matrices to identify data imbalances and unobserved factors that could disproportionately impact low-income communities (e.g., evaluated in public benefits fraud detection and child welfare case studies).

Qualitative evaluation of expected performance disparities using the 'Disparate Performance' matrix to conceptually identify and mitigate unequal outcomes across gender groups during the early AI ideation phase.

Assessment of unobserved contextual factors using the 'Model Unobservables' matrix, highlighting the necessity of human experts to identify and filter culturally biased AI outputs before they reach users (e.g., in LLM-generated educational content).

Evaluation of expected performance disparities across different languages due to unequal training data availability, assessed using the 'Disparate Performance' matrix (e.g., in language learning and translation AI concepts).
